## Perito Moreno Glacier

An exciting tour to Perito Moreno, a glacier considered one of the most accessible in the world and recognized by UNESCO as part of humanity's natural heritage. Perito Moreno is an immense mass of ice as tall as a 25-story building, covered by a 60-meter layer of moving ice.

You can watch the glacier from numerous observation platforms along the nearby shore. Perito Moreno can also be seen from the water on a boat safari. For a more adventurous experience, put on special crampons and walk on the glacier itself, peering into its blue caves on a "Mini-Trekking" excursion.

At times, it becomes difficult to see where the horizon lies between the ice and the sky. Approximately every 4 years, Perito Moreno Glacier blocks the channel between Lakes Argentino and Rico, preventing water from flowing between them. Meltwater accumulating in Lake Rico creates enormous pressure on the ice, eventually breaking through the ice dam and forming a tunnel within the glacier. Over the next two or three days, the tunnel widens until a huge arch collapses into the water with a thunderous roar. This is one of the world's most fascinating natural spectacles.

The excursion includes an English-speaking guide and private transfer.

Duration: 8-9 hours • Start: 9:00 – 9:30 a.m.

• Languages: English and Spanish

Step into the world of the ancient Maya. Today's journey takes you deep into the heart of the Yucatán Peninsula, where time seems to slow and echoes of the past still whisper through the trees. Begin the day at Uxmal, one of the most beautiful and refined cities of the ancient Maya. Explore the majestic Pyramid of the Magician, the magnificent Governor's Palace and the elegant Nunnery Quadrangle, each revealing the remarkable craftsmanship, astronomy and ceremonial life of this once-thriving civilization. To end the day, refresh yourself with a swim in a cenote, a sacred natural pool tucked away in the jungle. These crystal-clear waters were once revered by the Maya and still offer peace, refreshment and a touch of magic.

 Tour highlights:

● Explore the magnificent ruins of Uxmal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

● Hear the stories of ancient dynasties and sacred architecture from a certified guide.

● Swim in a cenote, a naturally formed pool of crystal-clear freshwater that was sacred to the Maya.

● Round-trip transportation and expert commentary are included for a seamless day.

 Included: Shared transportation, certified bilingual guide, admission to Uxmal and the cenote

Not included: Meals, tips, personal expenses

Today, journey into the fascinating world of the ancient Maya and visit some of the most impressive archaeological sites on the Yucatán Peninsula.
The excursion begins at Uxmal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its refined architecture and splendid decorative details. Walk through this ancient city and see its main landmarks, including the famous Pyramid of the Magician, the majestic Governor's Palace and the intricately decorated Nunnery Quadrangle. These structures reveal the high level of Maya artistic achievement, their knowledge of astronomy and their religious and ceremonial life.
Next, travel to the nearby archaeological site of Kabah, known for its impressive stone facades adorned with elaborate carvings and numerous masks of Chaac, the rain god.
The day ends with a refreshing stop at a cenote, a natural freshwater pool hidden among tropical vegetation. Such places held sacred significance for the ancient Maya. Here, you can relax and swim in crystal-clear water while enjoying the surrounding nature.

The route crosses the scenic high-altitude Altiplano, passing Laguna Colorada, whose reddish tones come from mineral deposits and the pink flamingos that inhabit it; the Sol de Mañana geyser field, located at more than 4,900 meters above sea level; and the Polques hot springs. Along the way, see the colorful Blanca and Verde lagoons at the foot of Licancabur Volcano. The border crossing and the entire journey to San Pedro de Atacama take approximately 8–9 hours.

The first stop is the Train Cemetery on the outskirts of Uyuni. Old steam locomotives and railcars have stood here since the region's mining industry expanded.

In Colchani, learn about salt mining and processing, activities closely tied to the lives of local residents. The route then reaches Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat. Its white surface stretches to the horizon; here you can clearly see the "water eyes," where water seeps through the salt crust.

On the way, enjoy panoramas of Tunupa Volcano. Visit Chantani Museum, dedicated to the region's natural and cultural heritage, and Incahuasi Island, also called Fish Island in the itinerary. Giant cacti several meters tall grow on its rocky slopes.

Lunch is served right on the salt flat, at a table surrounded by the white expanse. After lunch, continue the journey with stops to admire the landscapes and take photographs.

In the evening, return to the salt flat for tea at sunset. The white plain shifts in color from gold to pink and lilac, bringing the excursion to an end.
